top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Iran and the Ukraine war lead a heavy news evening. Iran began a week of state funerals as Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei, killed in February, lay in state in Tehran, while Tehran warned tankers to keep to approved Strait of Hormuz routes. Ukrainian officials called Russia's overnight assault on Kyiv the 'most massive' this year, with at least 30 killed. Europe's deadly heatwave eased but left thousands of excess deaths, Trump again questioned US support for NATO, and rescuers pulled a survivor from Venezuela's quake rubble after eight days.

stories.headline: Khamenei lies in state in Tehran as Iran begins week of funerals
stories.summary: The body of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei — killed in February during the conflict with Israel — lay in state at a Tehran religious complex as the country began days of official mourning and mass funeral events. Large crowds gathered across the capital.

stories.headline: 'Most massive' Russian attack on Kyiv kills at least 30
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities said Russia launched its 'most massive' assault on Kyiv this year, killing at least 30 people and wounding dozens — the deadliest strike on the capital in 2026. Rescue crews searched rubble as the toll rose; the figures are Ukrainian official counts.

stories.headline: France records thousands of excess deaths as European heatwave eases
stories.summary: France recorded about 2,025 excess deaths at the peak of the heatwave, the BBC reported, while The Straits Times cited at least 3,700 excess deaths across France, Belgium and the Netherlands as the extreme heat began to ease. Officials warned Europe faces more frequent extreme-heat events.

stories.headline: Iran warns tankers to use approved Strait of Hormuz routes or face 'forceful response'
stories.summary: Iran warned that oil tankers must stick to approved routes through the Strait of Hormuz or face a 'forceful response', according to Iranian authorities, keeping shipping on edge even as post-war traffic resumes. The warning was not independently corroborated by other governments.

stories.headline: Trump calls US support for NATO 'ridiculous'; Merz pushes back
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said it was 'ridiculous' for the United States to maintain its current level of support for NATO, renewing doubts over the American security commitment. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz responded that Germany can defend its military-spending push, as European allies move to fill gaps.

stories.headline: Ukrainian woman named by Interpol as main suspect in Monaco bomb attack
stories.summary: Interpol named a Ukrainian woman who fled to Germany as the main suspect in a bomb attack in Monaco, investigators said. Authorities are pursuing her as inquiries into the blast continue.

stories.headline: Venezuela quake survivor pulled out alive after eight days
stories.summary: Rescuers in Venezuela pulled a survivor from the rubble alive eight days after a powerful earthquake, as search teams hunted for any last signs of life. Authorities faced criticism over the disaster response, which the interim government defended.

stories.headline: Bomb blast at Damascus cafe kills nine, Syrian authorities say
stories.summary: A bomb blast tore through a cafe in Damascus, killing nine people, Syrian state media said. Authorities said an investigation was under way; no group had immediately claimed responsibility.

stories.headline: At least 32 dead after overcrowded bus plunges into ravine in Pakistan
stories.summary: At least 32 people were killed when an overcrowded bus plunged into a ravine in Pakistan, officials said. Poor road conditions and overloading are frequent factors in such crashes.

stories.headline: UN warns of strong looming El Nino
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that a strong El Nino is set to develop, raising the risk of extreme weather including heavier rain in some regions and drought in others. Agencies urged governments to prepare for the impacts on food and water security.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Cyber safety dominates the local day: about 70,000 people had data compromised in a breach involving SLA's cloud vendor IBM, even as police stood up a new SPF Cyber Command to disrupt scams and Citibank warned of phishing e-mails. Expect a wet, stormy night — NEA forecasts thundery showers with highs near 33°C. Bigger-picture plans landed too: a master plan to remake Greater Sentosa and Pulau Brani, up to 1,200 homes for Jurong Lake District, and closer ties with Timor-Leste, whose workers Singapore will hire from mid-2027. In the buzz, tributes poured in for Pek Kio's viral 'Stick Art Uncle', who died at 83. COE premiums fell at the latest exercise.

stories.headline: Data of 70,000 people compromised in cyber incident involving SLA vendor IBM
stories.summary: The Singapore Land Authority said the personal data of about 70,000 people was compromised in a cybersecurity incident involving a cloud environment run by its vendor, IBM. Affected individuals are being notified; SLA said it is working with IBM and the authorities to investigate.

stories.headline: New SPF Cyber Command aims to be 'tip of the spear' against scams
stories.summary: The Singapore Police Force launched a new Cyber Command to target scammers and cybercriminals before they reach victims, consolidating anti-scam and cybercrime capabilities. Police said it will focus on disruption and faster response as scam losses mount.

stories.headline: Greater Sentosa master plan unveiled with new attractions and revamped beaches
stories.summary: The Government unveiled a master plan to transform Greater Sentosa and Pulau Brani with new attractions, revamped beaches, canopy walks, trams and an islet-hopping experience, with works to be ready from the early 2030s. Officials framed it as a long-term boost to tourism.

stories.headline: Up to 1,200 private homes planned for Jurong Lake District site launched for sale
stories.summary: A Jurong Lake District site launched for sale could yield up to 1,200 private homes alongside office space and a town-hall link, as the district's build-out continues. The tender is part of Singapore's push to develop the area as a second CBD.

stories.headline: Singapore firms can hire Timorese workers from mid-2027; PM Wong honoured by Timor-Leste
stories.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore will open selected sectors such as construction to Timor-Leste work-permit holders from mid-2027, as the two countries deepen economic ties. Timor-Leste conferred its top honour on Mr Wong for Singapore's contributions to its nation-building.

stories.headline: Eminent Frog Porridge owner charged with S$3.8m tax evasion, money laundering
stories.summary: The owner of the well-known Eminent Frog Porridge restaurant was charged with evading about S$3.8 million in taxes and with money-laundering offences, with assets including a Lamborghini and S$2.4 million in cash listed in claims. The case is before the courts.

stories.headline: Citibank Singapore warns of e-mail phishing scams
stories.summary: Citibank Singapore warned customers about phishing e-mails impersonating the bank and urging recipients to click links or share credentials. It advised customers not to act on such messages and to verify communications through official channels.

stories.headline: Child taken to hospital after fire breaks out in Yishun HDB flat
stories.summary: A child was taken to hospital after a fire broke out in a Yishun HDB flat, the authorities said. The blaze was put out and the cause was being investigated.

stories.headline: 'Rest easy, Uncle': Pek Kio's viral twig artist Y.L. Thien dies at 83
stories.summary: Tributes poured in for Y.L. Thien, the 83-year-old 'Stick Art Uncle' known for crafting intricate art from twigs in Pek Kio, who has died. Residents and admirers remembered his gentle presence and the joy his creations brought the neighbourhood.

stories.headline: Actress-host Eswari Gunasagar speaks out after AI-generated fake images surface
stories.summary: Local actress-host Eswari Gunasagar spoke out after AI-generated fake images of her circulated on Facebook, calling the deepfakes distressing and urging platforms to act. The case adds to concern over AI-manipulated images of public figures in Singapore.

stories.headline: Actress Fiona Xie makes surprise appearance in viral TikToker's video
stories.summary: Actress Fiona Xie made a surprise cameo in a video by viral TikToker Tokyo Sims, delighting fans and fuelling online chatter. The clip spread quickly across local social media.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Russia's war on Ukraine escalated sharply: Ukrainian officials called Moscow's overnight assault on Kyiv the 'most massive' this year, with at least 30 killed, even as Poland's PM said Kyiv wants to lower tensions and the EU sanctioned six over Alexei Navalny's death. The US–Israel–Iran front is in a fragile post-war phase — Iran held state funerals for Supreme Leader Khamenei, killed in February, while warning tankers over Strait of Hormuz routes as flights resume. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers took over a Palestinian family's home as Gaza's loose ceasefire holds.

theatres.name: Russia–Ukraine War
theatres.status: Escalating — Ukraine reports its deadliest strike on Kyiv this year (≥30 killed, 3 Jul); diplomacy stalled.

timeline.event: Ukrainian authorities said Russia launched its 'most massive' assault on Kyiv this year, killing at least 30 people and wounding dozens (Ukrainian official count).
Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Ukraine wants to lower tensions and should confront history, as allies push diplomacy.
A Russian jobs website posted an advertisement for drone operators to defend Moscow, amid Ukrainian long-range drone attacks on Russian regions.
The EU issued sanctions against six people it linked to the death of Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, beginning the largest land war in Europe since 1945 (context).

theatres.name: US/Israel–Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Fragile post-war calm — Iran holds state funerals for Khamenei; issues fresh Hormuz shipping warning as flights resume.

timeline.event: The body of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, killed in February, lay in state in Tehran as Iran began a week of official mourning and mass funeral events.
Iran warned oil tankers to use approved routes through the Strait of Hormuz or face a 'forceful response', Iranian authorities said (not independently corroborated).
A BBC visit to the Strait of Hormuz found seized ships and an uneasy calm as post-conflict shipping slowly returns to normal.
Cathay Pacific said it would resume Middle East flights as US–Iran talks proceed, a sign of normalising conditions.

theatres.name: Israel–Gaza
theatres.status: Loose ceasefire holding; friction persists in the West Bank.

timeline.event: In the occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers took over a Palestinian family's home, the BBC reported, underscoring persistent friction despite the Gaza ceasefire.
Israel and Hamas agreed a US-brokered ceasefire that largely paused full-scale fighting after two years of war; strains have persisted since (context).

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic in DR Congo and Uganda is the gravest active outbreak — WHO confirmed 915 cases and 234 deaths as of mid-June and says numbers are rising rapidly, as a trial of Ebola treatments begins in DRC. India is managing a single confirmed Nipah case in Kerala under tight contact tracing, and WHO warns of rising yellow fever transmission across Africa and the Americas. One bit of good news: WHO says the cruise-ship hantavirus cluster is now over.

outbreaks.name: Bundibugyo Ebola — DR Congo & Uganda
outbreaks.status: Spreading rapidly; treatment trial under way
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO-confirmed only, DR Congo + Uganda combined (DRC 896 cases, 232 deaths, CFR ~26%; Uganda 19 cases, 2 deaths), per WHO DON608 (19 Jun 2026, data to 17–18 Jun). WHO says cases and deaths are rising rapidly; more-recent counts run higher but are not yet WHO-ratified, and suspected cases exceed confirmed.

outbreaks.name: Nipah virus — Kerala, India
outbreaks.status: Single confirmed case; contact tracing under way
outbreaks.scope_note: One lab-confirmed case in Kozhikode, Kerala (symptom onset 30 May), per WHO DON609 (25 Jun 2026). Nipah has a high case-fatality rate (historically 40–75%); contacts are under monitoring.

outbreaks.name: Hantavirus (MV Hondius) — declared over
outbreaks.scope_note: MV Hondius cruise-ship cluster: 12 confirmed + 1 probable case, 2 confirmed + 1 probable death (CFR 23%); all 13 among ship travellers, with contacts followed up across 33 countries/territories, per WHO DON611. WHO says the point-source outbreak no longer poses a public-health risk; no further transmission expected.

stories.headline: Ebola treatment trial begins in DR Congo as Bundibugyo outbreak spreads
stories.summary: A trial of Ebola treatments has begun in DR Congo as the Bundibugyo virus epidemic spreads. WHO's latest confirmed count is 915 cases and 234 deaths across DR Congo (896 cases, 232 deaths) and Uganda (19 cases, 2 deaths) as of mid-June, and it says numbers are rising rapidly.

stories.headline: WHO says cruise ship-linked hantavirus outbreak is over
stories.summary: WHO reported that the hantavirus cluster linked to the MV Hondius cruise ship is over, with a final tally of 13 cases (12 confirmed, one probable) and three deaths. It said the point-source outbreak no longer poses a public-health risk and no further transmission is expected.

stories.headline: WHO confirms Nipah virus case in Kerala, India
stories.summary: WHO confirmed a laboratory-positive Nipah virus case in Kozhikode, Kerala, with symptom onset on 30 May. Extensive contact tracing is under way given Nipah's high fatality rate and potential for person-to-person spread.

stories.headline: WHO warns of rising yellow fever transmission across Africa and the Americas
stories.summary: WHO's latest outbreak notice warns of sustained yellow fever transmission in Africa and a notable rise in the Americas, including spread into areas with low vaccination coverage. From January to May 2026 it recorded 16 confirmed cases in three African countries and 79 in six countries in the Americas, and urged stronger surveillance and immunisation.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Actively-exploited flaws lead this cycle: CISA added a Microsoft SharePoint RCE to its KEV catalog after in-the-wild attacks, and Cisco confirmed exploitation of a Unified CM flaw. AI and developer tooling are squarely in the crosshairs — attackers weaponised a Langflow RCE for automated ransomware, and researchers found sandbox-escaping flaws in the Cursor editor plus a critical unpatched Argo CD bug that could hand over Kubernetes clusters. Adobe shipped seven maximum-severity (CVSS 10) ColdFusion and Campaign fixes, and a pre-auth RCE in Kemp LoadMaster is under attack. Google disrupted the 2-million-device NetNut proxy network, and Pegasus spyware again hit an EU lawmaker. Patch SharePoint, Cisco, Adobe, Citrix NetScaler and Kemp LoadMaster now.

stories.headline: European Parliament member investigating spyware was hacked with Pegasus
stories.summary: Citizen Lab found that a former Member of the European Parliament who sat on a committee investigating spyware abuse had his phone repeatedly infected with NSO Group's Pegasus. The case renews scrutiny of commercial surveillance tools targeting officials in the bloc.

stories.headline: India investigates Tata data leak that exposed Apple iPhone secrets
stories.summary: India is investigating a data leak at Tata that reportedly exposed confidential Apple iPhone manufacturing information, according to CNA. The breach raises supply-chain confidentiality concerns for a key Apple assembly partner.

stories.headline: PamStealer uses fake Maccy sites and PAM checks to steal Mac login passwords
stories.summary: A new macOS infostealer dubbed PamStealer spreads via fake sites mimicking the Maccy clipboard app and abuses PAM (pluggable authentication module) prompts to capture users' login passwords. Mac users should download software only from trusted sources.

stories.headline: Google disrupts NetNut residential proxy network spanning 2 million home devices
stories.summary: Google said it significantly degraded NetNut, one of the largest networks that turns home devices into rented traffic relays abused to hide malicious activity. The disruption affects an estimated two million devices.

stories.headline: ConsentFix and ClickFix: how Microsoft 365 accounts are hijacked in seconds
stories.summary: Researchers detailed 'ConsentFix' and 'ClickFix' techniques that trick users into approving malicious OAuth consent or pasting attacker commands, hijacking Microsoft 365 accounts in seconds. Defenders should restrict app consent and user-initiated script execution.

stories.headline: ToddyCat-linked Umbrij malware abuses OAuth to access Gmail via Google API
stories.summary: A new malware family dubbed Umbrij, linked to the ToddyCat espionage group, abuses OAuth tokens to read victims' Gmail through the Google API, researchers said. The technique blends into legitimate cloud traffic to evade detection.

stories.headline: Cisco confirms attackers exploiting Unified CM SSRF flaw
stories.summary: Cisco confirmed active exploitation of a server-side request forgery flaw (CVE-2026-20230, CVSS 8.6) in Unified Communications Manager; CISA has added it to its KEV catalog. Administrators should apply Cisco's fixes and restrict exposed services.

stories.headline: AI agent exploits Langflow RCE to automate database ransomware attacks
stories.summary: Attackers are weaponising a remote-code-execution flaw in the Langflow AI app-builder — earlier abused to drop miners — now using an AI agent to automate ransomware against exposed databases. Exposed Langflow endpoints should be patched and taken offline.

stories.headline: FortiBleed credential-theft campaign linked to INC and Lynx ransomware
stories.summary: A credential-theft campaign dubbed 'FortiBleed', targeting Fortinet devices, has been tied to the INC and Lynx ransomware operations, researchers said. Stolen credentials are being used for initial access ahead of encryption.

stories.headline: New ChocoPoC RAT targets vulnerability researchers via fake PoC repos
stories.summary: A new RAT called ChocoPoC is spreading through trojanised proof-of-concept exploit repositories aimed at security researchers, echoing past targeting of the security community. Researchers should vet PoC code before running it.

stories.headline: Microsoft SharePoint RCE added to CISA KEV after active exploitation
stories.summary: CISA added a Microsoft SharePoint Server remote-code-execution flaw (CVE-2026-45659, deserialization of untrusted data, CVSS 8.8) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirmed in-the-wild attacks. Administrators should patch affected SharePoint servers immediately.

stories.headline: Medtronic notifies customers hit by ShinyHunters data breach
stories.summary: Medical-device maker Medtronic began notifying customers affected by a breach tied to the ShinyHunters extortion group, part of a wider wave of data-theft attacks. The exposed data and full scope are still being assessed.

stories.headline: Unpatched Argo CD repo-server flaw could let attackers take over Kubernetes clusters
stories.summary: Researchers disclosed an unpatched flaw in Argo CD's repo-server component that could let attackers compromise Kubernetes clusters. With no fix yet available, teams are urged to restrict exposure and monitor for abuse.

stories.headline: 19-year-old Scattered Spider suspect extradited to face US hacking charges
stories.summary: A 19-year-old alleged member of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group was extradited to the United States to face hacking charges. The group is tied to a string of high-profile social-engineering intrusions.

stories.headline: Adobe patches seven CVSS 10.0 flaws in ColdFusion and Campaign Classic
stories.summary: Adobe released fixes for seven maximum-severity (CVSS 10.0) vulnerabilities in ColdFusion and Campaign Classic that could allow remote code execution and system compromise. Given the perfect-score ratings, administrators should apply the updates urgently.

stories.headline: Critical Cursor flaws could let prompt injection escape sandbox and run commands
stories.summary: Researchers found flaws in the Cursor AI code editor that could let a prompt-injection attack escape its sandbox and execute commands on a developer's machine. It underscores growing risk in AI-assisted developer tooling; users should update.

stories.headline: Progress Kemp LoadMaster pre-auth RCE flaw faces active exploitation
stories.summary: A pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaw in Progress Kemp LoadMaster is drawing active exploitation attempts, researchers warned. Internet-facing load balancers should be patched and access restricted.

stories.headline: AI-generated browser ransomware abuses Chromium API across platforms
stories.summary: Researchers detailed AI-generated ransomware that abuses a Chromium browser API to encrypt files across Windows, Linux, macOS and Android. The proof-of-concept highlights how generative AI is lowering the bar for cross-platform malware.

stories.headline: Kubota says hackers had month-long access to network systems
stories.summary: Equipment maker Kubota disclosed that hackers had access to its network systems for about a month before being detected, and is investigating what data was affected. It said it is notifying affected parties as the probe continues.

stories.headline: Azure CLI password spray hits 78 Microsoft accounts in 81M+ attempts
stories.summary: A large password-spraying campaign abusing the Azure CLI made more than 81 million login attempts and compromised at least 78 Microsoft 365 accounts, researchers said. Organisations should enforce MFA and monitor for CLI-based authentication abuse.

stories.headline: DHS confirms hackers breached HSIN information-sharing platform
stories.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security confirmed attackers breached its Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN), used to share sensitive information with partners. DHS said it is investigating the scope of the intrusion.

stories.headline: Citrix patches six NetScaler flaws allowing file read and denial-of-service
stories.summary: Citrix released fixes for six NetScaler ADC and Gateway vulnerabilities that could enable unauthorized file reads and denial-of-service. Given NetScaler's history as an attacker target, prompt patching is advised.

stories.headline: Microsoft warns poisoned MCP tool descriptions can make AI agents leak data
stories.summary: Microsoft warned that maliciously crafted Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool descriptions can manipulate AI agents into leaking data, a fresh supply-chain-style risk for agentic AI. It urged validating and pinning trusted MCP tool definitions.
